The full workings live in `03-bv-by-arm.qmd`; the community-composition
context comes from `02-community-composition.qmd`. This page is the version
to present: the answer, the figure and table that carry it, and the
one-liner for the slides.

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)

source(here("R/count_tables.R"))

dd <- read_counts("group_b")
md <- dd$metadata
```

## The answer

**No.** BV affects roughly **43–49%** of participants in *every* arm, and
the differences between arms are what chance produces (Fisher p ≈ 0.45).
No contraceptive method in this study is associated with more or less BV.

## Figure 1 — BV status by arm: same story everywhere

```{r}
md |>
  count(arm, bv) |>
  ggplot(aes(arm, n, fill = bv)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Share of samples", fill = "BV status",
       title = "BV status by contraceptive arm — no arm stands out")
```

## Figure 2 — the label means what it says

If the `bv` column is trustworthy, BV-positive samples should carry more
*Gardnerella*, the genus most associated with bacterial vaginosis. Each
point is one sample; the y-axis is compressed to show all of them.

```{r}
tax <- dd$taxonomy
gardnerella <- colSums(dd$species[tax$Genus == "Gardnerella", ]) / colSums(dd$species)

md |>
  mutate(gardnerella = gardnerella[sample_id]) |>
  ggplot(aes(bv, gardnerella, colour = bv)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.6, size = 1.5) +
  scale_y_sqrt() +
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "crossbar", colour = "black", width = 0.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("negative" = "grey60", "intermediate" = "orange",
                                 "positive" = "firebrick"), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "BV status", y = "Gardnerella share of reads (sqrt scale)",
       title = "Gardnerella tracks the BV label — the label is safe to use")
```

## The evidence, in one table

```{r}
# 1. does the bv column agree with the Nugent score it should derive from?
nugent_cut <- cut(md$nugent, c(-Inf, 3, 6, Inf),
                  labels = c("neg", "intermediate", "pos"))
expected   <- recode(md$bv, negative = "neg", intermediate = "intermediate", positive = "pos")
mismatches <- sum(nugent_cut != expected)

# 2. the counts and the tests
t3 <- table(md$arm, md$bv)
fisher3 <- fisher.test(t3)$p.value
fisher2 <- fisher.test(table(md$arm, md$bv != "negative"))$p.value
prev <- md |>
  mutate(any_bv = bv != "negative") |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(share = scales::percent(mean(any_bv), 0.1)) |>
  deframe()

# 3. gardnerella medians (the sanity check behind Figure 2)
gard <- md |>
  mutate(gardnerella = gardnerella[sample_id]) |>
  group_by(bv) |>
  summarise(med = scales::percent(median(gardnerella), 0.1)) |>
  deframe()

tibble(
  claim = c("BV column vs Nugent score: mismatches",
            paste0("BV-positive or intermediate, by arm (",
                   names(prev)[1], " / ", names(prev)[2], " / ", names(prev)[3], ")"),
            "Arm and BV status, three categories (Fisher)",
            "Arm and BV status, positive vs not (Fisher)",
            "Gardnerella share, BV-positive vs negative (median)"),
  number = c(
    as.character(mismatches),
    paste(prev, collapse = " / "),
    paste0("p = ", round(fisher3, 2)),
    paste0("p = ", round(fisher2, 2)),
    paste0(gard[["positive"]], " vs ", gard[["negative"]])
  ),
  evidence = c("Anatomy-style label check",
               "Contingency table",
               "Fisher's exact test, `03-bv-by-arm`",
               "Fisher's exact test, `03-bv-by-arm`",
               "Biology check, `03-bv-by-arm`")
) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Claim", "Number", "Where it comes from"))
```

## Why this matters for the other question

Yesterday's ordination found BV status is the dominant structure in these
communities (R² ≈ 13%, p = 0.001) while arm explains almost nothing
(R² ≈ 3%, p ≈ 0.1). If BV had clustered in one arm, that arm's community
difference would have had a boring explanation. It did not: BV is spread
evenly, so it is a **rival explanation** for community patterns but **not a
confounder** of the arm comparison — and the suggestive pill-vs-injectable
signal from `02-community-composition` cannot be explained away as "the
pill arm simply had less BV". (If anything, the pill arm had the *least*.)

## The one-liner for the slides

> BV affects 43–49% of participants in every arm (Fisher p ≈ 0.45); the
> labels validate against Nugent scores and *Gardnerella* abundance. No
> method is associated with more or less BV — so BV, the main driver of
> community composition, is a rival explanation but not a confounder.

## Choices made

- All methods are inherited from `03-bv-by-arm.qmd`; nothing was re-decided
  here — this page only re-presents them.
- Main test **Fisher's exact test**, chosen because two table cells held
  fewer than 5 samples; chi-square agreed (p ≈ 0.47 / 0.84).
- Ran the test **both ways** — three BV categories, and positive-vs-not;
  the alternative was to pick one and hope.
- Treated **`intermediate` as not BV** in the two-category version;
  lumping it with positive instead moves the shares to 49% / 46% / 46%
  and changes nothing.
- Kept **all 93 samples**, including the nine low-depth ones: BV status
  comes from Nugent scoring, not sequencing depth, so shallow samples are
  still valid rows here.
- Figures and table **recompute** their numbers from the raw data rather
  than copy-pasting, so they would visibly disagree if `03-bv-by-arm.qmd`
  were changed.
